extracted.intended_audience: patent office administrators, FIPS/Rospatent staff, patent attorneys, IP educators and trainers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria for designing, delivering and evaluating patent-office educational, awareness-raising, conference and patent-analytics services (FIPS/Rospatent context). Covers intern training, continuing professional development, distance learning, thematic meetings, outreach and analytics product features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-specific patent attorney training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for patent attorney certification must undergo dedicated programs tailored to specific IP subject-matter areas (e.g., trademarks/service marks/appellations of origin; inventions and utility models; computer programs/databases/topographies of integrated circuits; industrial designs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report lists separate programs and student numbers for each subject area (examples: 45 graduates in trademarks program, 47 in inventions/utility models, 13 in programs/databases/topographies, 8 in industrial designs). Design curriculum by IP object specialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert-intern program structure and contact hours
rubrics_metrics.description: An "Expert-intern" program should combine extensive theoretical and practical experience by having interns work in expert units under experienced mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program specifications include defined academic hours (e.g., 232 academic hours for training experts examining inventions and utility models; 126 academic hours for training experts examining trademarks). Most trained interns are assigned full-time to expert departments upon completion, used as an effectiveness metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous professional development from hiring onward
rubrics_metrics.description: FIPS employees should participate in a unified continuous education system starting from the first day of employment, aimed at improving professional skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus training on new normative legal acts and procedural amendments (e.g., amendments to provisions on patent and other fees). Delivery formats include departmental technology-training sessions and group lessons; example statistics: 7 group sessions (420 specialists) and 252 departmental sessions in 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and state accreditation of educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary vocational and professional retraining programs must be delivered under proper license and state accreditation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: activities carried out under license series 77Л 01 No. 0008944 (reg. No. 038110) and state accreditation (State Accreditation Certificate No 3311 dated Jan 13, 2020). Ensure formal registration and accreditation of programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program development and quality assurance via Scientific and Technological Council
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced training and professional retraining programs should be developed and approved by the Office's Scientific and Technological Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2019, 25 advanced training programs and 3 professional retraining programs were developed/approved. Use leading FIPS state IP experts and external specialists/practitioners as teachers to raise program quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical orientation and teacher qualification as evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational programs should be practically oriented and delivered by highly qualified teachers; graduate feedback and employment outcomes should be used to evaluate program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduates emphasize relevance and practical orientation; high proportion of expert-interns assigned to expert departments is cited as evidence of effectiveness. Use participant feedback and placement rates as KPIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and expansion of distance learning programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Office training must include and expand distance learning offerings covering practical IP topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of distance programs launched: "Introduction to the technology transfer", "Building regional brands", "Recommendations on managing the rights in the results of intellectual activity and means of individualization" (for regional administrations), and "Commercial and regulatory specifics of pharmaceuticals turnover in the framework of IP rights protection". Track participation (including remote attendees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Central coordination of education via a Scientific Educational Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Create/co-locate a central coordinating body (Scientific Educational Center) to manage and coordinate educational activities across the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Center coordinated programs and trained 1092 specialists in 2019 (1069 under advanced training, including 55 by distance learning). Use a center to develop curricula, track outcomes, and liaise with corporate/university partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic meetings coverage: electronic filing and Office services
rubrics_metrics.description: Thematic meetings should instruct applicants and stakeholders on electronic filing procedures and Office e-services (e.g., ARM Registrar, "Your Account").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example topics included electronic filing of trademarks, inventions, appellations of origin using ARM Registrar; meetings dedicated to the "Your Account" service. Hold multiple targeted sessions (the report cites six meetings on ARM Registrar and two on e-filing for industrial designs/computer programs/databases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic meetings coverage: patent analytics and search tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Train stakeholders on patent analytics methods and how to use FIPS search systems and external tools for conducting IP searches and analytics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings/topics include "Patent analytics lounges", "Using the patent analytics when patenting inventions, utility models and industrial designs", and "Specific aspects of using search systems on the FIPS website". Provide hands-on demonstrations of search systems (DesignView, TMView cited elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on state registration of computer programs and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instruction on the legal and procedural specifics of state registration for computer programs and databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include seminars/webinars describing registration steps, documentation requirements and practical case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on international systems: Hague System for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses and meetings should cover submission and examination of industrial design applications under the Hague System for International Registration of Industrial Designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss international procedural differences and document requirements for Hague filings and examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized examination topics: IT and biotechnology
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specialized examiner training for sector-specific examinations, including IT technologies and biotechnology (sequence listings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include "Examination of applications in the IT technology field" and "Listing sequences of nucleotides and amino acids when characterizing inventions in the biotechnological field". Teach use of WIPO Sequence software and compliance with WIPO Standard ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on using technological analytics for public programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Train stakeholders to apply technological analytics to inform participation in state development programs and policy decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer sessions showing how analytics feed into strategic decision-making for regional/sectoral programs and investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for preparing analytical reports on inventive activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a standardized methodology for preparing analytical reports about inventive activity, IP and technological development for regional and sectoral administrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach data sources, indicators, patent analytics methods, presentation formats and policy-relevant interpretations for administrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on industrial design and trademark substantive/practice issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover current issues and common practice problems for patenting industrial designs and recognizing trademarks as well-known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include case reviews, common errors and strategies to improve filings and examinations in these domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and error-prevention for appellations of origin and registry amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Train applicants and practitioners on common mistakes when filing for appellations of origin and on procedures for state registration of exclusive rights deposition and making amendments to the State Registry and Certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical checklists and examples of frequent procedural/documentary errors to avoid during filings and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness-raising activities: targets and formats for youth outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Design youth-oriented IP awareness projects to develop inventive thinking, IP literacy and project-management skills among school and university students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: seminars/webinars on patent search, information resources, legal protection, submission algorithm; projects like "Inventors NEXT" and "Scientific Youth on Intellectual Property"; use webinars, face-to-face seminars, competitions, exhibitions and school visits. Track participation metrics and publish materials publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library and community outreach standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage the library community and other civic partners through webinars, exhibitions and published materials to popularize IP knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include webinar series with published materials (4553 views cited), exhibition projects, mobile and virtual exhibitions and cooperation with networks like "Quantorium" and "Sirius".

rubrics_metrics.name: Event/Conference design: diverse program formats and interactive elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize conferences with a mix of plenary sessions, working sections, partner/foreign sections, dedicated analytics days, business games, pitch-sessions and interactive modules to maximize impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 2.0 International Conference had 2 plenary sessions, 19 working sections, 7 partner sections, Patent Analytics Day, business games, pitch-sessions, AR modules, art-shows and excursions. Combine technical content with networking and startup-investor opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition-stand service standards
rubrics_metrics.description: At forums and exhibitions, Office stands should provide presentation materials/handouts and consulting services to visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rospatent stands provided materials and consulting at eight forums in 2019. Ensure staffing and materials to answer public inquiries and distribute informational handouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive information support and media strategy for events
rubrics_metrics.description: Events should have integrated information support: prepare press releases, announcements, interviews and publish content on Office websites and social networks to amplify reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report lists volumes of content published (e.g., 603 articles on Rospatent website, 849 on FIPS website) and media metrics (Rospatent: 22,048 media references). Include video materials, online broadcasting and track view/engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital transformation to improve public services
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt blockchain and artificial intelligence methods to enhance public service delivery—reducing processing times, increasing availability, transparency and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office is implementing blockchain and AI pilots as part of digital transformation; conferences and programs discuss these initiatives. Consider pilots, measurable KPIs and stakeholder communication when implementing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent analytics product standard: insight-driven, practical recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent analytics products should deliver in-depth technical analysis of valuable technologies/products and provide tailored, practical recommendations to customers on strategic responses (e.g., product development or market launch by competitors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIPS Project Office emphasizes insight-managed analytics for client-specific technological priorities, providing actionable recommendations that clients used to adjust R&D, assess financing prospects and identify technologies for foreign markets. Use sectoral expertise (oil/gas, transport, chemical, metallurgy, ICT) and case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and corporate/university cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate and deliver educational and analytics services in cooperation with corporate customers and universities across regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of corporate partners: Russian Railways, Gazprom, Roscosmos, Rosatom; training conducted in multiple cities (Novy Urengoy, Tomsk, Saint-Petersburg, Nizhny Tagil). Use partnerships to scale programs and ensure practical relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access of training/webinar materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Make webinar and seminar materials publicly accessible online and track viewership to extend impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Webinar materials were published and viewed thousands of times (example: 4553 views). Maintain online repositories (office websites, YouTube) and measure engagement.
